title: Sandboxing and resource limits
goals: Explain the mechanism and terminology of sandboxing and resource limits
Apply the stated procedure to a new case with a traceable result
Identify an assumption or limitation and design a revealing follow-up
vocabulary: An enforced restriction on process capabilities
Rules for accepting work under limits

blocks.text: A job requests a public webpage and a write outside its output directory.
Both operations violate the sandbox contract. Deny them; public availability does not grant network or filesystem authority.

independent_case.title: Apply a new case independently
independent_case.task: Queue currently has 9 tasks; job proposes 2 more under a maximum10 policy. Decide.
independent_case.answer: Teacher explanation: Accepting both would produce11 and exceed quota. Either reject the two-task batch or use a separately declared partial-admission policy; do not invent one.
independent_case.source: primary source W4, first curriculum occurrence

misconceptions: The worked result establishes every future case
Resource limits constrain execution but cannot prove generated claims or algorithms correct.
A missing input may be replaced without recording the change
A replacement changes the evidence or contract. Record the change and its justification; do not silently turn unknown into a measured value.
Repeating an assessed case is new independent evidence
A replay checks consistency. An example used for feedback or revision cannot later be described as untouched final evaluation.

blocks.text: The fictional job may read its fixture directory, write its output directory, use no network and run for at most 2 seconds with at most 10 queued tasks. Reject excess work before starting it.
